meta.title: Use ticket numbers for parent and dependency links

before.body:
## Problem
Tickets now display simple numbers such as #0, but parent and dependency validation compares incoming links directly against internal WB identifiers. The main ticket argument can use a number while links still require looking up the internal identifier.

## Intended behavior
Accept a numeric ticket reference such as "0" or "#0" for parent and dependency inputs, resolve it to the canonical internal ID before validation and persistence, and keep supporting existing WB identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Creating a child with --parent 0 or --parent '#0' succeeds for an existing ticket.
- Updating parent and dependency links accepts the same numeric string forms, including zero.
- Stored links and context use stable canonical IDs; existing links remain unchanged.
- Missing references, self-dependencies, and parent cycles are rejected.
- Focused tests cover create, update, resolution, and rejection behavior.
- CLI documentation includes a short numbered-reference example.

## Implementation starting points
src/store.ts: createNow, updateNow, validate, get.
src/cli.ts: create --parent and update --patch.

## Review evidence expected
Describe the before/after behavior, list tests run and their results, and identify any limits. Submit to Review rather than Done.
[![image.png](/api/images/image-8a5573e72e5dd781/base)](#image=image-8a5573e72e5dd781)

meta.title: Fix automatic service startup from the outer repository

after.body:
## Finding

When the local service is stopped, running the outer ControlRoomDev launcher with a command such as ./workboard list fails to start it. The child process imports tsx by package name from the inherited working directory, but node_modules now lives inside ControlRoom/.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced from ControlRoomDev against an empty temporary board. The command exited 1 with "Service did not start"; its service log contained ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package tsx imported from the outer kanbantool directory. The existing live service was not stopped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the TypeScript loader relative to the tool installation, independently of the caller working directory.
- [ ] With no service running, list/show and MCP can start and connect from the outer repository and another caller directory.
- [ ] Preserve startup for installed bundled JavaScript builds and source checkouts.
- [ ] Add an integration test that starts from a directory without node_modules and cleans up its temporary service.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/client.ts:129](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/client.ts#L129) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

## Review context

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

meta.title: Run MCP verification in the agent checkout

after.body:
## Finding

startMcp assigns cwd = store.root. The canonical board directory is used for verification commands, default claim paths, branch detection, and commit collection, even when the agent is working in a submodule or a separate worktree. In this project, the board repository is ControlRoomDev while application code is in ControlRoom/.

## Reproduction and evidence

Started the MCP process from a nested agent-checkout directory against a temporary shared board. submit_review with the harmless command pwd recorded the board root as both verification.cwd and output, rather than the launch directory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Keep canonical board storage separate from the agent execution directory.
- [ ] Use the agent checkout for verification, default claims, branch detection, and commits_since, with a documented way to specify it.
- [ ] Starting MCP in a submodule or linked worktree still reaches the shared board but verifies code in that checkout.
- [ ] Add integration coverage that distinguishes board and code directories and confirms the recorded branch/commits belong to the code checkout.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/mcp.ts:32](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/mcp.ts#L32) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

meta.title: Treat signal-terminated verification as a failure

after.body:
## Finding

runVerification converts a null process status to exit code 0 when result.error is absent. A command killed by a signal can therefore be submitted as successful verification and shown as passing in the ticket.

## Reproduction and evidence

In a disposable test, runVerification("kill -TERM $$", temporaryDirectory) returned exitCode: 0 with empty output. The command terminates only its own spawned shell; no application service was affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only an actual normal zero exit is recorded as a pass.
- [ ] Signal termination, timeout, and spawn errors produce failure evidence with a useful diagnostic.
- [ ] Both CLI and MCP reject failed verification unless the existing explicit failure override is used; overridden evidence remains visibly failed.
- [ ] Add focused tests for successful exit, nonzero exit, and signal termination.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/client.ts:296](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/client.ts#L296) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

## Review context

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

meta.title: Include approved scope instructions in agent briefs

after.body:
## Finding

contextMarkdown includes the parent and approved scope titles, but omits their bodies. Agents using next_ticket or get_context cannot see acceptance criteria, constraints, or exclusions kept on the approved parent, even when requesting a full Markdown brief.

## Reproduction and evidence

Created an approved parent whose description restricted work to a parser and prohibited renderer changes, then requested the child Markdown context. The parent title appeared but the scope description was absent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Include the approved scope description and acceptance criteria in Markdown context, with its identifier and attribution/reference.
- [ ] Include relevant parent context when the direct parent differs from the approved ancestor, without duplicating the same record.
- [ ] Brief mode must preserve approval boundaries and exclusions rather than silently dropping them.
- [ ] Test direct and ancestor approval through the Markdown API/MCP context paths.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/store.ts:871](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/store.ts#L871) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

meta.title: Keep matching parent tickets visible when filtering

after.body:
## Finding

In a view grouped by parent, the parent is represented by the group header instead of an item. Filtering drops every group with zero matching children, including groups whose parent itself matched the search.

## Reproduction and evidence

Created a parent titled Unique parent name and a differently named child. Filtering for Unique parent name produced one matching record but zero rendered groups. This also affects searches by the parent ticket number.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retain a group when its parent matches the active filter, even if none of its children match.
- [ ] Keep the parent visible and openable without falsely reporting no matches.
- [ ] Preserve child-only matches and the intended handling of genuinely empty groups.
- [ ] Add browser coverage for parent-title and parent-number searches in parent-grouped views.

## Source

meta.title: Allow MCP requests while waiting for ticket updates

after.body:
## Finding

The stdio request loop awaits each tool call before reading the next request. A long wait_for_update blocks unrelated reads, claim renewals, pings, and cancellation notifications on the same connection until it finishes.

## Reproduction and evidence

Against a disposable board, sent wait_for_update followed by get_ticket. The lookup remained unanswered while waiting; both responses arrived only after a comment released the wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch independent MCP requests without blocking the input reader and correlate each response with its request ID.
- [ ] get_ticket and ping respond while a wait_for_update request remains pending.
- [ ] Handle cancellation and connection closure so pending waits clean up their event streams and timers.
- [ ] Keep coordinated mutations serialized by the existing shared service and add concurrent-request regression coverage.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/mcp.ts:464](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/mcp.ts#L464) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

## Review context

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

meta.title: Fix generated CLI commands and hash-prefixed ticket IDs

after.body:
## Finding

Generated agent instructions contain commands such as workboard claim #3, where the shell treats #3 and the rest of the line as a comment. Quoting the number still fails in CLI paths because an unencoded # becomes a URL fragment. The shared wait helper also interpolates IDs without encoding.

## Reproduction and evidence

Read the generated protocol commands in contextMarkdown. A read-only invocation of ./workboard show '#0' against the live board returned "400: Invalid record ID", despite ticket #0 existing. MCP tools encode most IDs, but wait_for_update uses the shared unencoded wait helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generate shell-safe commands using plain numeric arguments such as workboard claim 3.
- [ ] Encode ticket identifiers when constructing CLI and shared wait API paths, preserving quoted #0, plain 0, and internal ID support.
- [ ] Test read, mutation, and wait paths with hash-prefixed IDs, and verify generated command examples actually work in a non-interactive shell.
- [ ] Coordinate with existing ticket #3, which covers parent/dependency field resolution; this ticket covers command arguments, generated instructions, and URL encoding.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/store.ts:948](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/store.ts#L948) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

meta.title: Allow MCP requests while waiting for ticket updates

before.body:
## Finding

The stdio request loop awaits each tool call before reading the next request. A long wait_for_update blocks unrelated reads, claim renewals, pings, and cancellation notifications on the same connection until it finishes.

## Reproduction and evidence

Against a disposable board, sent wait_for_update followed by get_ticket. The lookup remained unanswered while waiting; both responses arrived only after a comment released the wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch independent MCP requests without blocking the input reader and correlate each response with its request ID.
- [ ] get_ticket and ping respond while a wait_for_update request remains pending.
- [ ] Handle cancellation and connection closure so pending waits clean up their event streams and timers.
- [ ] Keep coordinated mutations serialized by the existing shared service and add concurrent-request regression coverage.

meta.title: Fix generated CLI commands and hash-prefixed ticket IDs

before.body:
## Finding

Generated agent instructions contain commands such as workboard claim #3, where the shell treats #3 and the rest of the line as a comment. Quoting the number still fails in CLI paths because an unencoded # becomes a URL fragment. The shared wait helper also interpolates IDs without encoding.

## Reproduction and evidence

Read the generated protocol commands in contextMarkdown. A read-only invocation of ./workboard show '#0' against the live board returned "400: Invalid record ID", despite ticket #0 existing. MCP tools encode most IDs, but wait_for_update uses the shared unencoded wait helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generate shell-safe commands using plain numeric arguments such as workboard claim 3.
- [ ] Encode ticket identifiers when constructing CLI and shared wait API paths, preserving quoted #0, plain 0, and internal ID support.
- [ ] Test read, mutation, and wait paths with hash-prefixed IDs, and verify generated command examples actually work in a non-interactive shell.
- [ ] Coordinate with existing ticket #3, which covers parent/dependency field resolution; this ticket covers command arguments, generated instructions, and URL encoding.

meta.title: Fix automatic service startup from the outer repository

before.body:
## Finding

When the local service is stopped, running the outer ControlRoomDev launcher with a command such as ./workboard list fails to start it. The child process imports tsx by package name from the inherited working directory, but node_modules now lives inside ControlRoom/.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced from ControlRoomDev against an empty temporary board. The command exited 1 with "Service did not start"; its service log contained ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package tsx imported from the outer kanbantool directory. The existing live service was not stopped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the TypeScript loader relative to the tool installation, independently of the caller working directory.
- [ ] With no service running, list/show and MCP can start and connect from the outer repository and another caller directory.
- [ ] Preserve startup for installed bundled JavaScript builds and source checkouts.
- [ ] Add an integration test that starts from a directory without node_modules and cleans up its temporary service.

- [ ] Starting MCP in a submodule or linked worktree still reaches the shared board but verifies code in that checkout.

meta.title: Fix automatic service startup from the outer repository

before.body:
## Finding

When the local service is stopped, running the outer ControlRoomDev launcher with a command such as ./workboard list fails to start it. The child process imports tsx by package name from the inherited working directory, but node_modules now lives inside ControlRoom/.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced from ControlRoomDev against an empty temporary board. The command exited 1 with "Service did not start"; its service log contained ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package tsx imported from the outer kanbantool directory. The existing live service was not stopped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the TypeScript loader relative to the tool installation, independently of the caller working directory.
- [ ] With no service running, list/show and MCP can start and connect from the outer repository and another caller directory.
- [ ] Preserve startup for installed bundled JavaScript builds and source checkouts.
- [ ] Add an integration test that starts from a directory without node_modules and cleans up its temporary service.

meta.title: Allow MCP requests while waiting for ticket updates

before.body:
## Finding

The stdio request loop awaits each tool call before reading the next request. A long wait_for_update blocks unrelated reads, claim renewals, pings, and cancellation notifications on the same connection until it finishes.

## Reproduction and evidence

Against a disposable board, sent wait_for_update followed by get_ticket. The lookup remained unanswered while waiting; both responses arrived only after a comment released the wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch independent MCP requests without blocking the input reader and correlate each response with its request ID.
- [ ] get_ticket and ping respond while a wait_for_update request remains pending.
- [ ] Handle cancellation and connection closure so pending waits clean up their event streams and timers.
- [ ] Keep coordinated mutations serialized by the existing shared service and add concurrent-request regression coverage.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/mcp.ts:464](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/mcp.ts#L464) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

before.body:

startMcp assigns cwd = store.root. meta.title: Treat signal-terminated verification as a failure

before.body:
## Finding

runVerification converts a null process status to exit code 0 when result.error is absent. A command killed by a signal can therefore be submitted as successful verification and shown as passing in the ticket.

## Reproduction and evidence

In a disposable test, runVerification("kill -TERM $$", temporaryDirectory) returned exitCode: 0 with empty output. The command terminates only its own spawned shell; no application service was affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only an actual normal zero exit is recorded as a pass.
- [ ] Signal termination, timeout, and spawn errors produce failure evidence with a useful diagnostic.
- [ ] Both CLI and MCP reject failed verification unless the existing explicit failure override is used; overridden evidence remains visibly failed.
- [ ] Add focused tests for successful exit, nonzero exit, and signal termination.

- Updating parent and dependency links accepts the same numeric string forms, including zero.
- Stored links and context use stable canonical IDs; existing links remain unchanged.
- Missing references, self-dependencies, and parent cycles are rejected.
- Focused tests cover create, update, resolution, and rejection behavior.

meta.title: Fix automatic service startup from the outer repository

before.body:
## Finding

When the local service is stopped, running the outer ControlRoomDev launcher with a command such as ./workboard list fails to start it. The child process imports tsx by package name from the inherited working directory, but node_modules now lives inside ControlRoom/.

## Reproduction and evidence

Reproduced from ControlRoomDev against an empty temporary board. The command exited 1 with "Service did not start"; its service log contained ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package tsx imported from the outer kanbantool directory. The existing live service was not stopped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolve the TypeScript loader relative to the tool installation, independently of the caller working directory.
- [ ] With no service running, list/show and MCP can start and connect from the outer repository and another caller directory.
- [ ] Preserve startup for installed bundled JavaScript builds and source checkouts.
- [ ] Add an integration test that starts from a directory without node_modules and cleans up its temporary service.

## Source

meta.title: Allow MCP requests while waiting for ticket updates

before.body:
## Finding

The stdio request loop awaits each tool call before reading the next request. A long wait_for_update blocks unrelated reads, claim renewals, pings, and cancellation notifications on the same connection until it finishes.

## Reproduction and evidence

Against a disposable board, sent wait_for_update followed by get_ticket. The lookup remained unanswered while waiting; both responses arrived only after a comment released the wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch independent MCP requests without blocking the input reader and correlate each response with its request ID.
- [ ] get_ticket and ping respond while a wait_for_update request remains pending.
- [ ] Handle cancellation and connection closure so pending waits clean up their event streams and timers.
- [ ] Keep coordinated mutations serialized by the existing shared service and add concurrent-request regression coverage.

## Source

before.body:
## Finding

startMcp assigns cwd = store.root. meta.title: Treat signal-terminated verification as a failure

before.body:
## Finding

runVerification converts a null process status to exit code 0 when result.error is absent. A command killed by a signal can therefore be submitted as successful verification and shown as passing in the ticket.

## Reproduction and evidence

In a disposable test, runVerification("kill -TERM $$", temporaryDirectory) returned exitCode: 0 with empty output. The command terminates only its own spawned shell; no application service was affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only an actual normal zero exit is recorded as a pass.
- [ ] Signal termination, timeout, and spawn errors produce failure evidence with a useful diagnostic.
- [ ] Both CLI and MCP reject failed verification unless the existing explicit failure override is used; overridden evidence remains visibly failed.
- [ ] Add focused tests for successful exit, nonzero exit, and signal termination.

meta.title: Use ticket numbers for parent and dependency links

before.body:
## Problem
Tickets now display simple numbers such as #0, but parent and dependency validation compares incoming links directly against internal WB identifiers. The main ticket argument can use a number while links still require looking up the internal identifier.

## Intended behavior
Accept a numeric ticket reference such as "0" or "#0" for parent and dependency inputs, resolve it to the canonical internal ID before validation and persistence, and keep supporting existing WB identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Creating a child with --parent 0 or --parent '#0' succeeds for an existing ticket.
- Updating parent and dependency links accepts the same numeric string forms, including zero.
- Stored links and context use stable canonical IDs; existing links remain unchanged.
- Missing references, self-dependencies, and parent cycles are rejected.
- Focused tests cover create, update, resolution, and rejection behavior.
- CLI documentation includes a short numbered-reference example.

## Implementation starting points
src/store.ts: createNow, updateNow, validate, get.
src/cli.ts: create --parent and update --patch.

## Review evidence expected
Describe the before/after behavior, list tests run and their results, and identify any limits. Submit to Review rather than Done.

after.body:
## Problem
Tickets now display simple numbers such as #0, but parent and dependency validation compares incoming links directly against internal WB identifiers. The main ticket argument can use a number while links still require looking up the internal identifier.

## Intended behavior
Accept a numeric ticket reference such as "0" or "#0" for parent and dependency inputs, resolve it to the canonical internal ID before validation and persistence, and keep supporting existing WB identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Creating a child with --parent 0 or --parent '#0' succeeds for an existing ticket.
- Updating parent and dependency links accepts the same numeric string forms, including zero.
- Stored links and context use stable canonical IDs; existing links remain unchanged.
- Missing references, self-dependencies, and parent cycles are rejected.
- Focused tests cover create, update, resolution, and rejection behavior.
- CLI documentation includes a short numbered-reference example.

## Implementation starting points
src/store.ts: createNow, updateNow, validate, get.
src/cli.ts: create --parent and update --patch.

before.body:
## Finding

runVerification converts a null process status to exit code 0 when result.error is absent. A command killed by a signal can therefore be submitted as successful verification and shown as passing in the ticket.

## Reproduction and evidence

In a disposable test, runVerification("kill -TERM $$", temporaryDirectory) returned exitCode: 0 with empty output. The command terminates only its own spawned shell; no application service was affected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only an actual normal zero exit is recorded as a pass.
- [ ] Signal termination, timeout, and spawn errors produce failure evidence with a useful diagnostic.
- [ ] Both CLI and MCP reject failed verification unless the existing explicit failure override is used; overridden evidence remains visibly failed.
- [ ] Add focused tests for successful exit, nonzero exit, and signal termination.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/client.ts:296](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/client.ts#L296) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

## Review context

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

before.body:
## Finding

Generated agent instructions contain commands such as workboard claim #3, where the shell treats #3 and the rest of the line as a comment. Quoting the number still fails in CLI paths because an unencoded # becomes a URL fragment. The shared wait helper also interpolates IDs without encoding.

## Reproduction and evidence

Read the generated protocol commands in contextMarkdown. A read-only invocation of ./workboard show '#0' against the live board returned "400: Invalid record ID", despite ticket #0 existing. MCP tools encode most IDs, but wait_for_update uses the shared unencoded wait helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generate shell-safe commands using plain numeric arguments such as workboard claim 3.
- [ ] Encode ticket identifiers when constructing CLI and shared wait API paths, preserving quoted #0, plain 0, and internal ID support.
- [ ] Test read, mutation, and wait paths with hash-prefixed IDs, and verify generated command examples actually work in a non-interactive shell.
- [ ] Coordinate with existing ticket #3, which covers parent/dependency field resolution; this ticket covers command arguments, generated instructions, and URL encoding.

## Source

[ControlRoom/src/store.ts:948](https://github.com/Quixotic7/ControlRoom/blob/07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19/src/store.ts#L948) at reviewed commit 07413cb4234f4ce7180a0126c21d6948c2311b19. Board repository: ControlRoomDev.

## Review context

Found during the 2026-09-26 Codex review. Type checking, 38 core/model tests, and 19 browser workflows passed; this case needs additional regression coverage.

## Finding

The stdio request loop awaits each tool call before reading the next request. A long wait_for_update blocks unrelated reads, claim renewals, pings, and cancellation notifications on the same connection until it finishes.

## Reproduction and evidence

Against a disposable board, sent wait_for_update followed by get_ticket. The lookup remained unanswered while waiting; both responses arrived only after a comment released the wait.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch independent MCP requests without blocking the input reader and correlate each response with its request ID.
- [ ] get_ticket and ping respond while a wait_for_update request remains pending.
- [ ] Handle cancellation and connection closure so pending waits clean up their event streams and timers.
- [ ] Keep coordinated mutations serialized by the existing shared service and add concurrent-request regression coverage.

## Finding

contextMarkdown includes the parent and approved scope titles, but omits their bodies. Agents using next_ticket or get_context cannot see acceptance criteria, constraints, or exclusions kept on the approved parent, even when requesting a full Markdown brief.

- [ ] Include relevant parent context when the direct parent differs from the approved ancestor, without duplicating the same record.
- [ ] Brief mode must preserve approval boundaries and exclusions rather than silently dropping them.
- [ ] Test direct and ancestor approval through the Markdown API/MCP context paths.

## Problem
Tickets now display simple numbers such as #0, but parent and dependency validation compares incoming links directly against internal WB identifiers. The main ticket argument can use a number while links still require looking up the internal identifier.

## Intended behavior
Accept a numeric ticket reference such as "0" or "#0" for parent and dependency inputs, resolve it to the canonical internal ID before validation and persistence, and keep supporting existing WB identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria
- Creating a child with --parent 0 or --parent '#0' succeeds for an existing ticket.
- Updating parent and dependency links accepts the same numeric string forms, including zero.
- Stored links and context use stable canonical IDs; existing links remain unchanged.
- Missing references, self-dependencies, and parent cycles are rejected.
- Focused tests cover create, update, resolution, and rejection behavior.
- CLI documentation includes a short numbered-reference example.

## Implementation starting points
src/store.ts: createNow, updateNow, validate, get.
src/cli.ts: create --parent and update --patch.

## Review evidence expected
Describe the before/after behavior, list tests run and their results, and identify any limits. Submit to Review rather than Done.

meta.title: Conversation sorts tickets with newest comments first

before.body:
This should sort oldest comments first with an icon you can click to change sort order. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Read a ticket’s conversation in chronological order by default, with a simple icon control to switch to newest-first when desired.

### Scope and approach

Default ticket conversations to oldest-first. Add a visible sort-direction icon next to Conversation with a tooltip, accessible name, and current order. Remember the selected preference per project. This controls comments inside a ticket, independently of the newest-first project activity feed in #25.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a conversation without an existing preference shows comments from oldest to newest, ordered by their recorded timestamps rather than filenames or record enumeration order.
- [ ] Clicking the sort control switches between Oldest first and Newest first; all comment types participate in the same consistent order.
- [ ] Equal timestamps use a deterministic secondary key, and changing order neither duplicates nor loses entries.
- [ ] The chosen order persists across closing/reopening and refresh through the project preference model.
- [ ] New comments appear in the correct position without forcing a reader away from older content; after posting, the author can readily find their own new comment.
- [ ] Keyboard users can toggle the icon, and its label/tooltip communicates the current order and available action. Existing comment resolution and review summaries continue to work.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect src/store.ts comments enumeration and web/RecordDetail.tsx conversation mapping, plus the existing preference plumbing in web/App.tsx and src/server.ts. Apply presentation sorting without changing stored timestamps or the chronological history available to agents.

### Human review / verification

Use a conversation with mixed comment types, deliberately nonchronological record filenames, and equal timestamps. Check the default, toggle both directions, post a comment, reload, and confirm no entry disappears or changes content.

meta.title: View tabs change horizontal size when selecting them

before.body:
I would like these to keep same horizontal width. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Keep each saved-view tab at the same width and position when selected so the tab strip does not shift under the pointer.

### Scope and approach

Reserve space for active-only controls and state indicators rather than changing tab width on selection. Preserve variable widths for different names; the requirement is stable width across selection states, not identical widths for all names.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Switching among Board, Table, and custom views does not change each tab’s measured width or shift neighboring tabs.
- [ ] Options controls and unsaved indicators fit within the reserved space without overlapping labels.
- [ ] Inactive hidden controls are not focusable, and active options remain usable with keyboard and pointer.
- [ ] Long names, renaming, overflow, comfortable/compact density, and light/dark appearance continue to work.
- [ ] A browser regression compares tab bounding boxes before and after selection with a small subpixel tolerance.

### Implementation notes and related work

web/ProjectPage.tsx currently mounts the options Menu only for the active tab. Inspect that markup and web/project.css view-tab styles for the width change before altering layout.

### Human review / verification

Repeatedly switch between short and long named tabs using pointer and keyboard; check that tab edges remain fixed and options/renaming still work.

### Intended outcome

Find and assign a parent by typing its title or ticket number instead of browsing an increasingly long dropdown.

### Scope and approach

Replace the parent selector with an accessible autocomplete. Show number, title, and stage in suggestions, the selected parent clearly, and an explicit No parent action. Typing a search query must not create a ticket or change the relationship until a result is selected.

Use a fixture with hundreds of tickets, duplicate titles, a ticket numbered 0, and nested parents. Confirm keyboard operation, correct disambiguation, and cycle rejection.

meta.title: When click a ticket for review, would be nice to have buttons to quickly move to done or fail review

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

When a human opens a ticket in Review, make Accept into Done and Request changes immediately available without changing a status dropdown.

### Scope and approach

Add prominent, distinct review outcome buttons in ticket detail, alongside the review summary and conversation. Request changes should target the configured Failed Review column when available; otherwise use an explicit project setting or visible choice of an appropriate progress column. Keep naming aligned with the board actions in #16.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a Review ticket, a human sees Accept into Done and Request changes with the destination clearly indicated; these do not appear as active agent acceptance actions.
- [ ] Accept into Done saves any pending ticket edits and moves to the configured Done destination using current revision checks.
- [ ] Request changes allows a concise review comment, saves it as human Review feedback, and moves the ticket to the configured return stage; submitting does not require a long questionnaire.
- [ ] If a save or transition fails, the ticket remains open with the draft/feedback retained and a clear error; retry does not duplicate feedback.
- [ ] A successful action closes the dialog consistently with Save and updates the board immediately, retaining previous handoff and verification history.
- [ ] Multiple custom Review/Done/progress columns are handled by explicit deterministic destination rules, and accepting a parent never silently accepts its children.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx save/close/review actions, src/store.ts authority/history, and project column configuration. Related: #16 provides quick actions outside the dialog; #18 handles status customization. Share action logic to avoid divergent validation.

### Human review / verification

Open a reviewed ticket, accept it and observe the board; repeat with Request changes and a comment. Test pending edits, a stale save, renamed columns, and missing Failed Review configuration. Check attribution and preservation of the review conversation.

meta.title: Have rules in the agent instructions to auto document decisions

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make decision documentation a routine part of the agent protocol so consequential project choices and their reasoning are retained beyond the originating ticket.

### Scope and approach

Update tool-neutral agent guidance, generated context, and MCP onboarding to instruct agents to look up existing decisions and create/update decision records when choosing a meaningful architecture, product behavior, UI convention, dependency strategy, or workflow policy. Keep routine implementation trivia out of the decision log.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Instructions state when to record a decision, with examples of consequential choices versus minor implementation details.
- [ ] A decision records the choice, context, rationale, alternatives considered, tradeoffs, scope, attribution, and links to relevant tickets/references.
- [ ] Agents search existing decisions before creating another, link tickets to the applicable decision, and supersede earlier decisions explicitly rather than rewriting away the old rationale.
- [ ] Unresolved proposals and assumptions are labeled as such; an agent does not invent human agreement or treat an unresolved question as an accepted choice.
- [ ] Agents may record decisions within approved work, but decision records do not grant implementation scope approval or bypass human acceptance of tickets.
- [ ] Review handoffs identify decisions made or changed, and agents can retrieve those records after the originating ticket is archived.
- [ ] The instructions ship consistently in AGENT_GUIDE.md, generated context, and MCP guidance; users can see the rule in the playbook from #26.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with AGENT_GUIDE.md, src/store.ts contextMarkdown and decision validation, src/mcp.ts onboarding/list_knowledge, and existing record create/update APIs. Reuse durable decision records and predecessor links. This is protocol-driven behavior, not automatic inference from arbitrary file changes.

### Human review / verification

Run a disposable agent workflow that makes a meaningful design choice, records its alternatives/rationale, links it to the ticket, and later supersedes it. Confirm the guidance is available through CLI/MCP context and that archived work does not hide its decisions.

meta.title: Bulk edit feature for tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Select multiple tickets and change shared fields in one operation, with predictable selection and a clear result for every ticket.

### Scope and approach

Extend the existing table checkbox/bulk-status UI to status, priority, owner, labels, and parent; expose selection on the board as well. Labels need separate add/remove actions so existing labels are not accidentally replaced. Approval actions are specified in #16; deletion is outside this ticket.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Board and table support explicit multi-selection, select visible items, clear selection, and a persistent count while the action is being prepared.
- [ ] Only selected visible tickets are affected; filtering or changing view reconciles selection and never silently includes hidden items.
- [ ] Mixed values display as Mixed. Fields left unchanged retain their original values; label addition/removal preserves all other labels.
- [ ] Each change uses the ticket’s revision and normal validation, including parent cycles, scope, and review evidence requirements.
- [ ] The result identifies succeeded, failed, and unchanged tickets; failed items remain available for correction/retry without reapplying successful writes.
- [ ] Selection and operations are keyboard accessible and survive ordinary live refresh without jumping to different tickets.

### Implementation notes and related work

web/TableView.tsx currently loops onMove for bulk status changes. Start there and in web/ProjectPage.tsx; coordinate shared selection/results rather than creating a second independent bulk model. Related: #16 and #23.

### Human review / verification

Bulk-edit a mixed selection, add/remove labels, and simulate a stale revision plus a validation failure. Verify exact affected IDs, preservation of untouched fields, and per-item feedback.

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Approve work from the board or table without opening each ticket. Make scope approval and acceptance of completed work separate, clearly named actions.

### Scope and approach

Provide Approve scope for unapproved planned work, and Accept into Done for tickets in Review. Show the result inline. Batch actions share the selection model from #17. Scope approval alone should not silently select, start, or complete a ticket.

- [ ] A human can approve a ticket’s scope from its card/row; approved and inherited-scope states are visually distinguishable.

- [ ] Agent requests cannot approve scope or accept work into Done, including through the new bulk path.
- [ ] Stale revisions and partial failures are shown per ticket; successful changes retain human attribution and do not overwrite unrelated fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

### Human review / verification

Approve scope on a single item and selected items, then accept a reviewed item. Check that status is unchanged by scope approval, agent calls remain rejected, and a stale item produces a clear result.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Show the prospective ticket order while dragging so the user knows where the ticket will land before releasing it.

meta.title: Have a view in which I can sort ticket priority by vertically reordering tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Provide a dedicated vertical planning view where dragging tickets changes the order in which work should be considered.

### Scope and approach

Build on the saved table view and existing manual/priority sorting. Offer an obvious Priority planning preset, rank tickets within priority groups, and allow explicit movement into another priority group. Ordering must not silently change workflow status or parent. Explain that priority is the urgency bucket and rank is the order within it.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The planning view shows a vertical list with priority groups and visible drag handles, including the start/end of each group.
- [ ] Dragging within a group changes persistent relative rank; dragging to another priority group updates priority and rank visibly.
- [ ] Reordering across tickets with different statuses does not move either ticket to the other status or change its parent.
- [ ] Move up/down and move-to-priority controls provide keyboard alternatives, including first/last positions.
- [ ] Reloading or returning to the saved view retains the order; concurrent reorder failures reconcile without losing tickets.
- [ ] Filtered reordering uses defined visible anchors and preserves the relative order of hidden tickets; saved sort modes clearly indicate whether manual reordering is active.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/ProjectPage.tsx place/peersOf, web/TableView.tsx and web/model.ts sortTickets. Current place also copies the target status, so reuse needs care. Coordinate drag preview with #22; prefer existing order metadata over a second competing ranking field.

### Human review / verification

Rank tickets across several stages and priorities, move to first/last, refresh, and repeat with a filter and keyboard controls. Confirm that status/parent stay unchanged and priority changes only when crossing an explicit priority group.

before.body:
These are just small tasks that are tracked inside the ticket and don't show up as separate full tickets. Sort of like a checklist of things that need to be done for that ticket. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Track small steps inside a ticket with a checklist, without creating separate numbered tickets or cluttering the board.

### Scope and approach

Provide an editable Microtasks section with add, rename, reorder, complete, and remove actions. Keep it readable/editable in Markdown and include it in agent context. Reuse Markdown task-list syntax in a clearly owned section where practical; preserve other prose and existing acceptance criteria.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enter adds a nonblank checklist item and keeps focus ready for the next; items can be checked, edited, reordered, and removed with keyboard alternatives.
- [ ] Items persist across save/reopen and direct Markdown edits; concurrent changes use revision protection.
- [ ] Agents can read and update checklist state through the supported record interfaces without creating ticket IDs for checklist items.
- [ ] The ticket displays completed/total counts, including the all-complete state; cards may show a compact count without listing every item.
- [ ] Completing the checklist does not automatically move the ticket to Done or claim its acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- [ ] Unrelated Markdown, attachments, and comments survive checklist edits.

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx, web/RecordMarkdown.tsx (GFM rendering already exists), src/files.ts Markdown preservation and src/store.ts context. Related: #14 for work large enough to need child tickets; #23 for reducing board clutter.

### Human review / verification

Create/reorder/toggle items, reopen, edit a task in Markdown, and retrieve agent context. Verify a stale toggle cannot overwrite a newer edit and all-complete leaves ticket status unchanged.

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

Settings already supports naming, roles, ordering, addition, and removal of columns. Expose a clear Customize statuses entry from the board and improve that existing editor. Retain stable IDs and explain why workflow roles control agent behavior; multiple columns can share a role, as Concept and Backlog do here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can find status customization from the board, add a status, rename it, and change its order without editing configuration files.
- [ ] Renaming or reordering retains ticket associations, history, and saved views; refreshing preserves the configuration.
- [ ] The editor distinguishes display name from workflow role and validates required roles and invalid/blank names.
- [ ] Removing a populated status offers an explicit destination/migration flow or a clear route to move its tickets first; no tickets are orphaned.
- [ ] Where a role has multiple columns, default destinations for new tickets and agent role-based moves are visible and deterministic.
- [ ] Concurrent configuration changes cause reconciliation feedback rather than silent overwrites.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/Settings.tsx, web/ProjectPage.tsx, src/store.ts updateConfig and role-to-column lookups in src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts. Extend existing configuration rather than introducing competing status data.

### Human review / verification

Add and rename a status, reorder it, reload, and remove an empty status. Exercise removal with tickets and ambiguous role destinations using Concept/Backlog and In Progress/Failed Review.

meta.title: Need a way to merge or relate tickets in case of duplicates

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Connect overlapping tickets and consolidate genuine duplicates without losing their discussion, images, decisions, or history.

### Scope and approach

Support a lightweight Related tickets relationship and a separate explicit merge action that chooses a surviving ticket. Show a reviewable merge preview. Retain the source ticket as an archived duplicate pointing to the survivor rather than deleting its record; preserve original attribution and links.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Find related tickets by number/title, add or remove a relationship, and see reciprocal links in both details and agent context without treating related work as a blocking dependency.
- [ ] A merge preview identifies the survivor and source, content to preserve, and conflicts in parent, status, owner, priority, or acceptance criteria; conflicting metadata is not silently overwritten.
- [ ] The survivor retains access to source descriptions, comments, attachments/annotations, and decision/rule references with their original provenance. Existing links to the source still resolve and show the survivor.
- [ ] Source tickets are explicitly marked as duplicates and excluded from ordinary active views after merge; this does not claim the work was completed or accepted into Done.
- [ ] Incoming parent/dependency links are handled deliberately, with cycle/self-link validation, and both records retain an audit trail.
- [ ] Merge uses revision checks on every affected record and reports partial failure/recovery clearly; repeated requests must not duplicate content. Related links remain independently editable.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with src/types.ts, src/store.ts relationship/context/archive behavior, and web/RecordDetail.tsx. Add CLI/MCP support so agents can identify duplicates and retrieve related context. Coordinate with #23; related, duplicate, parent, and dependency are distinct relationships.

### Human review / verification

Relate two tickets, then preview and merge duplicates containing different comments/images and conflicting metadata. Follow old links, retrieve agent context, and simulate stale input. Confirm that no content or attribution disappears and no ticket is falsely accepted as Done.

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer a newest-first project activity feed so a human can quickly see what changed across tickets and project knowledge.

meta.title: Figure out how to deal with bloat of too many tickets

before.body:
## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Keep a growing project understandable while retaining completed work, decisions, and historical context for humans and agents.

### Scope and approach

Start with a bounded design/discovery task: evaluate existing archive, filters, saved views, and parent grouping on a realistically crowded board; propose an explicit ticket lifecycle and focused follow-up changes. Use Concept for raw ideas, microtasks for small steps, and parent tickets for larger outcomes. Do not automatically delete or archive records as part of this investigation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the distinct sources of clutter: raw ideas, tiny tasks, duplicates, completed work, and large expanded parent groups.
- [ ] Demonstrate proposed default/focus/archive views with a representative fixture, showing how to find active work and retrieve older tickets.
- [ ] Specify explicit archive/unarchive behavior and any suggested bulk or completion-age controls, preserving links and discoverability.
- [ ] Check that decisions and UI rules remain available after their originating tickets are archived.
- [ ] Measure current board/search behavior on a documented large fixture and propose performance work only where measured behavior warrants it.
- [ ] Produce a reviewable recommendation with tradeoffs and a small ordered set of follow-up scopes; capture any unresolved product choices for human review.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect web/model.ts filters/grouping, web/ProjectPage.tsx saved views, and src/store.ts record/index/context behavior. Existing archive and is:archived filtering are starting points. Related: #17 bulk actions, #20 microtasks, #21 planning and #25 feed.

### Human review / verification

Walk through capturing an idea, promoting it, completing work, archiving/retrieving it, and finding a related decision on the representative board. Review the recommendation before scheduling implementation follow-ups.

meta.title: Tickets in progress should animate and track the agents progress

before.body:
If in progress would be nice to see how long llm has worked on ticket as well as estimated progress. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Make in-progress work easier to monitor with restrained animation, elapsed time, and agent-reported progress that clearly communicates uncertainty.

### Scope and approach

Show current owner/claim, last reported update, elapsed time since entering In Progress, and an optional agent-reported percentage or checklist progress. Elapsed wall-clock time is not measured active work. Running-agent supervision remains outside the initial product; animation must not imply a verified live process.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cards/rows and ticket details show last reported activity and elapsed time with explicit labels; reload reconstructs elapsed time from durable timestamps.
- [ ] Agents can report a short progress note and optional bounded percentage through CLI/MCP; percentages are labeled estimates, and missing values display as unknown rather than invented.
- [ ] Checklist completion, if shown from #20, is labeled separately from overall completion; 100% never automatically moves a ticket to Done.
- [ ] Expired claims, stale reports, and blockers are visibly distinct from recent reported activity; the UI never treats a claim alone as proof an agent is running.
- [ ] Subtle in-progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences and stops or changes appropriately for blocked/stale/review/done states.
- [ ] Repeated work sessions retain useful history; displayed elapsed duration uses a documented rule for leaving and re-entering In Progress, without double-counting or inventing active hours.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/TicketCard.tsx, web/TableView.tsx, src/types.ts, src/store.ts claims/history and CLI/MCP update interfaces. Prefer explicit reported data and disposable derived timers over writing a record every second. Related: #20 and #25.

### Human review / verification

Exercise a fresh report, missing estimate, stale/expired claim, blocker, and re-entry into In Progress with controlled timestamps. Reload and enable reduced motion; verify the labels never claim measured agent runtime.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Offer the requested retro and music-hardware-inspired themes while retaining the current Control Room appearance and readable, usable controls.

### Scope and approach

Treat this as an umbrella for a reusable theme structure and all requested presets: Win95, Win 3.1, Commodore 64, Classic Mac System 7, AmigaOS, NES, SNES, Synthwave, Elektron, and Gameboy. Keep System, Light, and Dark available. Develop representative previews first, then deliver presets in reviewable batches; this ticket is complete only when the agreed full set is available.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A theme picker presents clear names and previews and persists the selected theme with the existing preference model.
- [ ] Each requested preset has a coherent palette, typography, surfaces, borders, focus treatment, and semantic state colors; presets need more than a background-color swap.
- [ ] Board, table, ticket dialogs, conversation, knowledge views, menus, settings, and screenshot tools remain legible and usable in every preset.
- [ ] Keyboard focus, contrast, validation states, blocked/review states, and responsive layouts remain distinguishable without relying solely on color.
- [ ] Theme switching preserves application state and annotation geometry; System continues to follow the operating system appearance.
- [ ] Shared tokens and reusable overrides avoid duplicating application layout or behavior for each theme.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/styles.css tokens, web/project.css, web/TopNav.tsx themes, and web/App.tsx preference handling. Use original styling/assets inspired by the references. Create child implementation tickets when this umbrella is selected for development.

### Human review / verification

Review a consistent set of desktop/mobile screenshots for every preset and exercise keyboard focus, long content, error states, and reload persistence. Obtain visual review of representative presets before extending the full set.

Enable “Approve this scope for agent work” on this parent and click Save. Tell the agent when ready. At the end, inspect the child in Review and either accept Done or comment with requested changes.

meta.title: Conversation sorts tickets with newest comments first

before.body:
This should sort oldest comments first with an icon you can click to change sort order. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Read a ticket’s conversation in chronological order by default, with a simple icon control to switch to newest-first when desired.

### Scope and approach

Default ticket conversations to oldest-first. Add a visible sort-direction icon next to Conversation with a tooltip, accessible name, and current order. Remember the selected preference per project. This controls comments inside a ticket, independently of the newest-first project activity feed in #25.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a conversation without an existing preference shows comments from oldest to newest, ordered by their recorded timestamps rather than filenames or record enumeration order.
- [ ] Clicking the sort control switches between Oldest first and Newest first; all comment types participate in the same consistent order.
- [ ] Equal timestamps use a deterministic secondary key, and changing order neither duplicates nor loses entries.
- [ ] The chosen order persists across closing/reopening and refresh through the project preference model.
- [ ] New comments appear in the correct position without forcing a reader away from older content; after posting, the author can readily find their own new comment.
- [ ] Keyboard users can toggle the icon, and its label/tooltip communicates the current order and available action. Existing comment resolution and review summaries continue to work.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect src/store.ts comments enumeration and web/RecordDetail.tsx conversation mapping, plus the existing preference plumbing in web/App.tsx and src/server.ts. Apply presentation sorting without changing stored timestamps or the chronological history available to agents.

### Human review / verification

Use a conversation with mixed comment types, deliberately nonchronological record filenames, and equal timestamps. Check the default, toggle both directions, post a comment, reload, and confirm no entry disappears or changes content.

meta.title: Conversation sorts tickets with newest comments first

before.body:
This should sort oldest comments first with an icon you can click to change sort order. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Read a ticket’s conversation in chronological order by default, with a simple icon control to switch to newest-first when desired.

### Scope and approach

Default ticket conversations to oldest-first. Add a visible sort-direction icon next to Conversation with a tooltip, accessible name, and current order. Remember the selected preference per project. This controls comments inside a ticket, independently of the newest-first project activity feed in #25.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a conversation without an existing preference shows comments from oldest to newest, ordered by their recorded timestamps rather than filenames or record enumeration order.
- [ ] Clicking the sort control switches between Oldest first and Newest first; all comment types participate in the same consistent order.
- [ ] Equal timestamps use a deterministic secondary key, and changing order neither duplicates nor loses entries.
- [ ] The chosen order persists across closing/reopening and refresh through the project preference model.
- [ ] New comments appear in the correct position without forcing a reader away from older content; after posting, the author can readily find their own new comment.
- [ ] Keyboard users can toggle the icon, and its label/tooltip communicates the current order and available action. Existing comment resolution and review summaries continue to work.

### Implementation notes and related work

Inspect src/store.ts comments enumeration and web/RecordDetail.tsx conversation mapping, plus the existing preference plumbing in web/App.tsx and src/server.ts. Apply presentation sorting without changing stored timestamps or the chronological history available to agents.

### Human review / verification

Use a conversation with mixed comment types, deliberately nonchronological record filenames, and equal timestamps. Check the default, toggle both directions, post a comment, reload, and confirm no entry disappears or changes content.

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

meta.title: Add questionaires to tickets for human review

before.body:
If the LLM has questions about a ticket, they can add a questionaire with multiple choice questions or text questions to a ticket and mark it as needing human feedback. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Let an agent attach a structured questionnaire to a ticket and request human input, keeping questions and answers in the ticket’s conversation.

### Scope and approach

Support one or more multiple-choice or free-text questions, an explicit needs-feedback state, and answering at the human’s pace. Store structured data durably in Markdown records/metadata and expose it through CLI/MCP context. Keep this distinct from mandatory ticket creation forms.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An agent can submit a questionnaire with stable question IDs, clear prompts, answer types, and optional recommended choices; users can provide custom text where choices are offered.
- [ ] The ticket appears in Needs you with a direct route to its unanswered questionnaire; a separate flag does not silently change its workflow stage.
- [ ] Questions never time out or disappear because the user pauses. Draft answers persist across closing/reopening and refresh, and can be submitted explicitly.
- [ ] No recommended/preselected option counts as an answer until the human submits; required unanswered questions remain visible.
- [ ] Submitted answers retain human attribution, question wording, and timestamps in the conversation, and are readable by agent context and wait-for-update workflows.
- [ ] Question edits/replacements and amended answers retain history; stale submissions do not overwrite a newer questionnaire, and resolving one request does not clear unrelated open questions.

### Implementation notes and related work

Extend src/types.ts, src/store.ts comments/context, src/server.ts, src/cli.ts/src/mcp.ts, web/RecordDetail.tsx and web/model.ts attention handling. Reuse the existing question/resolve flow where possible. Related: #26.

### Human review / verification

Submit a mixed questionnaire, leave it unanswered beyond ordinary UI timers, save a partial draft, reload, and finish later. Confirm that an agent receives the explicit answers and that a concurrent question edit triggers reconciliation.

- [ ] Keyboard focus, contrast, validation states, blocked/review states, and responsive layouts remain distinguishable without relying solely on color.
- [ ] Theme switching preserves application state and annotation geometry; System continues to follow the operating system appearance.
- [ ] Shared tokens and reusable overrides avoid duplicating application layout or behavior for each theme.

meta.title: parent ticket box should be a text field with intellisense

before.body:
Once there's a lot of tickets this current dropdown list won't work. 

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Find and assign a parent by typing its title or ticket number instead of browsing an increasingly long dropdown.

### Scope and approach

Replace the parent selector with an accessible autocomplete. Show number, title, and stage in suggestions, the selected parent clearly, and an explicit No parent action. Typing a search query must not create a ticket or change the relationship until a result is selected.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Search matches title text and numeric references including 0 and #0, with a bounded suggestion list and an informative empty state.
- [ ] Arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape dismisses, and focus/selection are announced through combobox semantics.
- [ ] The current ticket and descendants cannot be selected as parents; server validation still rejects cycles and stale writes.
- [ ] An existing parent stays visible even if archived or excluded by current board filters; ordinary suggestions prioritize nonarchived tickets.
- [ ] Selecting, clearing, saving, reopening, and canceling a search preserve the expected relationship and unrelated ticket fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx parent selector, web/TagInput.tsx for existing suggestion patterns, and src/store.ts ticketLinks/validate. Related: #14. Store canonical IDs while displaying public ticket numbers.

### Human review / verification

Use a fixture with hundreds of tickets, duplicate titles, a ticket numbered 0, and nested parents. Confirm keyboard operation, correct disambiguation, and cycle rejection.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Find and assign a parent by typing its title or ticket number instead of browsing an increasingly long dropdown.

### Scope and approach

Replace the parent selector with an accessible autocomplete. Show number, title, and stage in suggestions, the selected parent clearly, and an explicit No parent action. Typing a search query must not create a ticket or change the relationship until a result is selected.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Search matches title text and numeric references including 0 and #0, with a bounded suggestion list and an informative empty state.
- [ ] Arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape dismisses, and focus/selection are announced through combobox semantics.
- [ ] The current ticket and descendants cannot be selected as parents; server validation still rejects cycles and stale writes.
- [ ] An existing parent stays visible even if archived or excluded by current board filters; ordinary suggestions prioritize nonarchived tickets.
- [ ] Selecting, clearing, saving, reopening, and canceling a search preserve the expected relationship and unrelated ticket fields.

### Implementation notes and related work

Start with web/RecordDetail.tsx parent selector, web/TagInput.tsx for existing suggestion patterns, and src/store.ts ticketLinks/validate. Related: #14. Store canonical IDs while displaying public ticket numbers.

### Human review / verification

Use a fixture with hundreds of tickets, duplicate titles, a ticket numbered 0, and nested parents. Confirm keyboard operation, correct disambiguation, and cycle rejection.

## Backlog refinement

Prepared by Codex backlog refinement. This describes planned work; implementation has not started.

### Intended outcome

Keep each saved-view tab at the same width and position when selected so the tab strip does not shift under the pointer.

### Scope and approach

Reserve space for active-only controls and state indicators rather than changing tab width on selection. Preserve variable widths for different names; the requirement is stable width across selection states, not identical widths for all names.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Switching among Board, Table, and custom views does not change each tab’s measured width or shift neighboring tabs.
- [ ] Options controls and unsaved indicators fit within the reserved space without overlapping labels.
- [ ] Inactive hidden controls are not focusable, and active options remain usable with keyboard and pointer.
- [ ] Long names, renaming, overflow, comfortable/compact density, and light/dark appearance continue to work.
- [ ] A browser regression compares tab bounding boxes before and after selection with a small subpixel tolerance.

### Implementation notes and related work

web/ProjectPage.tsx currently mounts the options Menu only for the active tab. Inspect that markup and web/project.css view-tab styles for the width change before altering layout.

### Human review / verification

Repeatedly switch between short and long named tabs using pointer and keyboard; check that tab edges remain fixed and options/renaming still work.
